findings.text: follow-on: the guard admits the memo whenever the run directory exists and is non-empty, a proxy for 'holds the run's records' rather than a test of it; a directory carrying any unrelated entry, or one left by another process, still receives the classification memo, and the predicate is a filesystem property a future writer could narrow silently. Low risk because the run directory is the run's own home and the memo is a best-effort cache; named so the boundary is on record.

follow-on: the reviewed run records its after_suite at revision 371d42bc3, one commit before the reviewed head b1336f1a9; the intervening commit (docs(evidence): drop a rot-prone line reference) edits only the evidence fragment, so the gate result transfers, but the gate as recorded was not run at the reviewed head. An independent head-arm run at b1336f1a9 reproduced it exactly (1 failed, 34 passed).

justifications.durability: The guard is exercised by three cases in the new file — absent directory, empty directory, and the positive control that a directory holding the run's records still receives the memo — so it does not rest on a passing suite; the node's own mutation log and my independent mutation both show the new code path, not incidental coverage, is what the cases measure. Docked two: the empty/non-empty predicate is a filesystem proxy a future writer could narrow silently (only the new cases would redden), and the memo is still written into any non-empty run directory regardless of who created it, so a directory left by an unrelated process would keep acquiring memos — a real but low-exposure boundary for a best-effort cache.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced on an extracted copy of the reviewed head under $TMPDIR, not by reading the node's logs: head arm at b1336f1a9 is 1 failed, 34 passed, EXIT=1 (the single failure tests/test_a_live_run_never_reads_dead.py::test_a_departure_with_no_ledger_evidence_keeps_the_promoted_word), base arm at 53f2c080f is 3 failed, 29 passed, EXIT=1 (the same id plus both named ids). The failure-id set difference head-minus-base is empty, so added_failure_count is 0 with no ids; the surviving failure is present at base and belongs to the departure-vocabulary work, not this node. My own mutation (guard removed, unconditional mkdir restored) turns the new file's two cases and both named ids red: 4 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1 — the guard is load-bearing. Logs carry revision, module `__file__` and cwd headers. Docked one because the node's recorded after_suite ran at 371d42bc3, one commit before the reviewed head b1336f1a9; the intervening commit edits only the evidence fragment, so the result transfers, but the gate as recorded was not run at the reviewed head.
justifications.fit: The change follows the module's idiom: a single early return and the deleted mkdir inside the existing best-effort atomic-write helper, the docstring rewritten to state the mechanism (a read must not bring a run's home into being), and no versioned or plan/ticket-labelled names introduced. The test module keeps the fixture-synthesis shape — its own scratch files, a fixed MOMENT so the reading cannot depend on wall clock, a foreign launcher_host so liveness comes from the record — and its three function names state what each case holds. Lint is clean on the new file.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The node's goal — classifying a pointer no longer creates or fills a run directory that did not exist — is met. `_write_classification_memo` now returns before opening its temp file unless the run's directory already exists and is non-empty (reckon/crew/recovery.py:5659, `if not path.parent.is_dir() or not any(path.parent.iterdir()): return`), and the unconditional `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` is deleted. Both named ids (tests/test_a_discard_never_reads_promoted.py::test_a_discarded_block_never_reads_promoted and tests/test_crew_discard_reads_discarded.py::test_a_discard_leaves_no_record_when_its_run_directory_is_gone) go red at base and green at head without either test file being edited — base..head touches exactly three paths, neither of them these two — so the fix repairs the product rather than the fixtures. The new file carries the required no-directory case plus an empty-home case and a positive control. Docked one because the guard tests 'non-empty directory' as a proxy for 'holds the run's records'; a run directory holding any unrelated entry still receives the memo.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exactly three paths differ across base..head, all inside the node's declared write paths: reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_a_classification_read_creates_no_run_directory.py and docs/evidence/fragments/the-suite-is-green-at-head/a-classification-read-creates-no-run-directory.html. No plan, index or sprint state is mutated; the worktree is clean at the reviewed head. The two named test files are deliberately left unedited. The new test relies on the suite's autouse RECKON_HOME fixture for isolation and leaves no artifacts in the real crew home (checked for r-nodir, r-empty, r-homed under the live pointer and runs directories — absent). Ruff adds no findings on either changed Python file; the nine findings in recovery.py are pre-existing and far from the edited region.
